subject: maths
question: A 12 litre solution of acid and water contains 30% acid. How much water (in litres) must be added to get a solution having 20% acid?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since only water is added, the quantity of acid remains constant.

Initial Volume × Initial Acid % = Final Volume × Final Acid %

12 × 30% = Final Volume × 20%

Final Volume = (12 × 30) ÷ 20 = 18 litres

Water added = Final Volume − Initial Volume = 18 − 12 = 6 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial solution = 12 litres

Initial Acid concentration = 30%

Final Acid concentration = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Quantity of constant component = Total Volume × Percentage concentration

 Alligation Method (Acid %)
 
 Initial: 30%
 
 Water: 0%
 
• 
 
• 
 
 20%
 
• 
 
• 
 20 − 0 = 20
 30 − 20 = 10
 Ratio = 2 : 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let water added be x litres.

⇒ Initial Acid quantity = 30% of 12 = 0.30 × 12 = 3.6 litres.

⇒ In the new solution, acid quantity is still 3.6 litres but represents 20% of the total.

⇒ 20% of (12 + x) = 3.6

⇒ (20 ÷ 100) × (12 + x) = 3.6

⇒ (1 ÷ 5) × (12 + x) = 3.6

⇒ 12 + x = 3.6 × 5

⇒ 12 + x = 18

⇒ x = 18 − 12 = 6 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concentration Formula

Concentration of a solution = (Quantity of solute ÷ Total volume of solution) × 100.

Constant Solute Principle

When only the solvent (like water) is added or evaporated, the absolute quantity of the solute (like acid or salt) remains unchanged: V₁C₁ = V₂C₂.

Alligation Rule

Ratio of two quantities = (Cheaper concentration − Mean concentration) : (Mean concentration − Dearer concentration).</p
